thread:
customer-admin: Hey team — LoopLabs private deployment (VPC) is seeing KMS failures since ~2026-03-15T22:00Z. App calls to /v1/kms/decrypt return 502 + occasional 'TLS handshake failure' in our proxy logs. We also saw an intermittent 'kms:AccessDenied' from the HSM-side. Need help triaging, customer in prod.
support-eng: Thanks — can you paste the proxy logs around a failure and confirm whether this is across all pods or single AZ? Also: any infra changes recently (egress allowlist, NAT/GW)?
customer-admin: Logs below (redacted). It's across 3 pods across 2 AZs. No infra change on customer side we know of. We did have a config push to the KMS routing policy yesterday but it was a minor timeoutext change.
```
Apr 15 22:03:12 proxy[pid]: upstream error: TLS handshake failed: SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL
Apr 15 22:03:12 proxy[pid]: downstream: 502, request: POST /v1/kms/decrypt
Apr 15 22:03:12 proxy[pid]: upstream response: kms-service: refused connection
Apr 15 22:03:14 proxy[pid]: upstream error: error from KMS: kms:AccessDenied for key arn:...
```
support-eng: Quick checklist — most common causes in private deployments: DNS resolving to wrong IP (private route53 / split-horizon), SNI mismatch (HSM expects specific server_name), missing SNAT / egress IP changes (HSM allowlist only sees NAT IPs), or mTLS client certs not being presented. Can you run these from a failing pod and paste output: 
```
# DNS
dig +short kms.looplabs.internal
# TLS
openssl s_client -connect $(dig +short kms.looplabs.internal):443 -servername kms.looplabs.internal -showcerts -state -debug
# simple curl
curl -v --resolve 'kms.looplabs.internal:443:$(dig +short kms.looplabs.internal)' https://kms.looplabs.internal/health
```
customer-admin: Ran them from pod 'api-3' — outputs: `dig` -> 10.2.3.4
`openssl` -> SSL_connect: `SSL routines:ssl3_get_server_certificate:certificate verify failed` and `verify error:num=19:self signed certificate in certificate chain`
`curl -v` -> TLS handshake error and then 502 after retry.
support-eng: Ok that suggests the TLS certificate chain presented by 10.2.3.4 doesn't chain to the customer's trust store OR the pod sees a different IP with a different cert. Two parallel possibilities: 1) traffic is going to a vendor-managed HSM that requires client mTLS and our client cert is not being presented, causing AccessDenied; 2) traffic is being SNATed through a public egress and the HSM sees an unexpected source IP and denies.
evan: FYI we rolled an egress allowlist update to HSM vendor last night for another customer. Could be related if the vendor applied a narrower policy. I'll check the change log.
oncall-bot: config-deploy-prod: egress-allowlist-update applied by infra-ci at 2026-03-15T21:45Z (change-id: egress-2026-090).
maria: From infra side — LoopLabs uses a NAT gateway with no SNAT rules on the pod network; pods use node IPs and we rely on customer-managed SNAT on their side. If the HSM only allows specific NAT IPs and the node IPs changed (scale or replacement), they'd see AccessDenied. Two next steps: confirm what source IP the HSM sees and confirm TLS SNI expected value.
support-eng: To confirm source IP (from a pod): `curl -s --connect-timeout 2 http://ifconfig.me` won't work in private; instead, run a tcpdump during a failed handshake and capture the SYN packets to get the source IP, or ask HSM vendor for connection logs. Example tcpdump: 
```
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 10.2.3.4 and port 443 -c 50 -w /tmp/hsm.pcap
# or print SYN packets
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0 and host 10.2.3.4' -c 20
```
customer-admin: Captured pcap attached (uploaded to ticket). Tcpdump shows source IPs 172.20.4.12 and 172.20.4.13 which are pod IPs (no NAT). HSM vendor says they only have a few NATed public IPs on their allowlist.
support-eng: That confirms SNAT is missing and HSM sees unexpected private IPs — vendor will reject. Two remediation options: a) enable SNAT at the cluster egress (preferred) so connections originate from a known NAT IP; or b) ask vendor to add the pod IP ranges (not ideal). Also need to address TLS cert chain: vendor indicated they rotated a leaf cert and require SNI to match exactly `kms.looplabs.internal`. If traffic bypasses SNI due to an L7 proxy rewriting Host header, you'll see cert mismatch.
evan: Adding — on some setups our sidecar proxy strips SNI when doing upstream TLS passthrough -> TLS termination mismatch. Check proxy config: make sure upstream_tls.server_name is set and that client cert/key (for mTLS) are mounted into the sidecar.
maria: I'd like these traces: 1) output of `env | grep -i TLS` from the pod, 2) sidecar config snippet for upstream TLS, 3) the pcap we received, and 4) HSM vendor connection logs (time + observed src ip + cert CN). I'll open an infra escalation.
support-eng: Repro steps we performed and ask customer to run (one-liner): 
```
# On a failing pod
kubectl exec -it api-3 -- sh -c "dig +short kms.looplabs.internal && openssl s_client -connect $(dig +short kms.looplabs.internal):443 -servername kms.looplabs.internal -showcerts -brief" > /tmp/kms-debug.txt
kubectl cp api-3:/tmp/kms-debug.txt ./kms-debug-api-3.txt
```
customer-admin: Ran the one-liner and attached kms-debug-api-3.txt. Confirmed sidecar config had `upstream_tls.server_name` blank due to config templating bug.
support-eng: That explains the cert mismatch. Action items: 1) customer to populate server_name in sidecar config and restart pods (rolling restart), 2) infra to enable SNAT or instruct vendor to add cluster NAT IPs, 3) we will coordinate with HSM vendor to whitelist the NAT IPs once provided.
evan: I'll rollback the templating change that cleared server_name for customers provisioned before 2026-03-10.
maria: I'll open infra ticket INFRA-4827 to enable SNAT for the LoopLabs cluster and link vendor escalation. Please attach the pcap and verify HSM can see source NAT IPs after change.
support-eng: Marking this thread escalated -> INC-2102. Hold for customer confirmation after server_name fix + SNAT. Happy to assist with probing after changes. :thumbsup:
customer-admin: Thanks — we'll patch sidecar, roll, and report back. Appreciate the quick triage.
